x: A great win for John Bicourt, who beat old rivals Cope, Church and Badgery in fine style. These four were well away and a full minute separated the first and fifth runners at the finish.

Badgery and Church,as expected,tore off into the lead,but Adrian ran a steadier race working his way through the field until just after the half-way mark he went into 3rd place which he held to the finish.
The two Norths then took well over a minute off Drewett and Badgery of Mitcham leaving Mel Thorpe to thoroughly enjoy himself by putting a further 350 yards between us and our rivals.

Left on his own for some time he probably felt in the latter stages that he would at least salvage second place, but the field had closed up alarmingly behind and in the last mile or so Barratt, Heaver, Franklin, and Briault all swept past with Badgery, Presland and Graham close behind.
Fastest times: Badgery (Mit) 16:51, Lightfoot (Read) 16:55, Stevens (Read) 17:02. CRANFORD (Thames Valley Harriers)---March 22nd

Just 2 months away from becoming a 40 yrs old veteran, Laurie O'Hara was faced with a situation where he had little to gain (Piotrowski and Badgery were well ahead) and everything to lose (T.V.H., Aldershot, Portsmouth and Cambridge were all within striking distance).
But Belgrave have their heroes too and Laurie O'Hara, chasing hard after Badgery of Hercules Wimbledon, took 34 seconds off of our rivals.
